---
description: "How often Island Transit's buses left on time, day by day and hour by hour, and how the figures are checked."
title: "On time"
subtitle: "The whole system, by hour, day, week or month"
---

::: {.method-note}
We work out these figures ourselves from the buses' live locations, so they
aren't Island Transit's official numbers. [Methods](methods.qmd) explains
how, and [Routes](routes.qmd) shows one route at a time.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, num, count, unit, band, lateness, longDate, hourLabel, plural, serviceDays, recentDays, withDates, showAllToggle, bandLegend, emptyNote, guard, h, MIN_OBSERVED, REPO_URL, DATA_URL, DATA_RAW_URL, RELEASES_URL, periodInput, periodName} from "./lib.js"
import {makeCharts, splitLegend} from "./charts.js"
import {Plot, d3} from "./vendor/plot-0.6.11/plot.js"
ch = makeCharts({Plot})
daily = csv(d3, "data/ontime/daily.csv")
// Days with scheduled service; a holiday is archived but not charted.
days = withDates(serviceDays(daily))
latestDate = days.length ? days.at(-1).day : null
latest = latestDate ? json(`data/ontime/days/${latestDate}.json`) : null
periods = json("data/ontime/periods.json")
// The daily table lists the day but its detail file did not load.
noDetail = () => days.length === 0 ? emptyNote("no-days") : emptyNote("unavailable", `The details for ${longDate(latestDate)}`)
```

## Over time

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof period = periodInput()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Off the Day view there is nothing to toggle; the empty element still
// holds a value, so the chart below does not wait for one.
viewof showAll = period === "day" ? showAllToggle(days.length) : Object.assign(h("span", {hidden: true}), {value: false})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// Hour of the day: the last 28 service days pooled (ontime/periods.json),
// or the latest day alone when that file is not there.
pooledHours = periods?.grains?.hour?.pooled
hourRows = pooledHours?.rows?.length ? pooledHours.rows : Object.entries(latest?.by_hour ?? {}).map(([hour, b]) => ({hour: +hour, ...b}))
hourSpan = pooledHours?.rows?.length
  ? (pooledHours.first_service_date === pooledHours.last_service_date ? `on ${longDate(pooledHours.last_service_date)}` : `from ${longDate(pooledHours.first_service_date)} to ${longDate(pooledHours.last_service_date)}, all service days together`)
  : `on ${longDate(latestDate)}`
hours = hourRows
  .map(b => ({...b, band: band(b?.on_time_share_of_observed, b?.observed), label: hourLabel(b.hour)}))
  .filter(d => d.observed >= MIN_OBSERVED && d.on_time_share_of_observed != null)
  .sort((a, b) => a.hour - b.hour)
```

::: {.slot-chart}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  if (period === "hour") {
    if (hours.length === 0) return noDetail();
    return ch.figure({
      note: `Departures ${hourSpan}, grouped by the hour each was scheduled, in Pacific time. We leave out any hour with fewer than ${MIN_OBSERVED} departures seen.`,
      legend: bandLegend(),
      chart: ch.bars(hours, {
        category: "label", value: "on_time_share_of_observed", upright: true, fill: d => d.band.color,
        axisLabel: "On time", references: [0.6, 0.8],
        ariaLabel: `Share of departures on time by scheduled hour, ${hourSpan}`,
        tip: d => `${d.label}\n${pct(d.on_time_share_of_observed)} on time\nTypically ${lateness(d.deviation_s_median)}\n${count(d.observed)} of ${count(d.scheduled)} departures seen`,
      }),
      tableLabel: "Show the hours as a table",
      table: ch.table(hours, {
        caption: `On-time figures by scheduled hour, ${hourSpan}`,
        columns: [
          {key: "label", label: "Hour", sortValue: d => d.hour},
          {key: "on_time_share_of_observed", label: "On time", align: "right", format: v => pct(v)},
          {key: "deviation_s_median", label: "Typical departure", align: "right", format: v => lateness(v)},
          {key: "observed", label: "Seen", align: "right", format: count},
          {key: "scheduled", label: "Scheduled", align: "right", format: count},
        ],
      }),
      methods: "on-time-performance",
    });
  }
  if (period === "week" || period === "month") {
    const rows = (periods?.grains?.[period] ?? []).filter(r => r.observed > 0)
      .map(r => ({...r, label: periodName(period, r.period) + (r.partial ? " (part)" : "")}));
    if (rows.length === 0) return emptyNote("unavailable", `The figures by ${period}`);
    const word = period === "week" ? "week (Monday to Sunday)" : "month";
    return ch.figure({
      note: `Every departure seen in each ${word}, early, on time and late. "Part" marks a ${period} the archive does not cover from start to end.`,
      legend: splitLegend(),
      chart: ch.stack(rows, {category: "label", ariaLabel: `Early, on time and late departures by ${period}`}),
      tableLabel: `Show the ${period}s as a table`,
      table: ch.table([...rows].reverse(), {
        caption: `On-time figures by ${period}`,
        columns: [
          {key: "label", label: period === "week" ? "Week" : "Month", sortValue: d => d.period},
          {key: "on_time_share_of_observed", label: "On time", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
          {key: "early_share_of_observed", label: "Early", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
          {key: "late_share_of_observed", label: "Late", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
          {key: "deviation_s_median", label: "Typical departure", align: "right", format: v => lateness(v)},
          {key: "days", label: "Days", align: "right", format: count},
          {key: "observed", label: "Departures seen", align: "right", format: count},
        ],
      }),
      methods: "on-time-performance",
    });
  }
  if (days.length === 0) return emptyNote("no-days");
  if (days.length < 2) return html`<p class="empty">So far there is one day of data, ${longDate(latestDate)}, and ${pct(days[0].on_time_share_of_observed)} of the departures we saw that day were on time.
      A day-by-day trend line will appear once a second day comes in.</p>`;
  const shown = recentDays(days, showAll);
  return ch.figure({
    chart: ch.trend(shown, {
      y: "on_time_share_of_observed", format: v => pct(v, 1), yLabel: "On time", height: 240,
      ariaLabel: "Share of departures on time, by service day",
      describe: `From ${longDate(shown[0].day)} to ${longDate(latestDate)}. On the latest day, ${pct(days.at(-1).on_time_share_of_observed)} of the departures seen were on time.`,
      tip: d => `${longDate(d.day)}\n${pct(d.on_time_share_of_observed, 1)} on time\n${pct(d.observed_share)} of departures seen`,
    }),
    tableLabel: "Show the days as a table",
    table: ch.table([...shown].reverse(), {
      caption: "Share of departures on time, by service day",
      columns: [
        {key: "day", label: "Service day", format: v => longDate(v)},
        {key: "on_time_share_of_observed", label: "On time", align: "right", format: v => pct(v, 1)},
        {key: "deviation_s_median", label: "Typical departure", align: "right", format: v => lateness(v)},
        {key: "observed", label: "Departures seen", align: "right", format: count},
        {key: "scheduled", label: "Scheduled", align: "right", format: count},
      ],
    }),
    methods: "on-time-performance",
  });
}, "The chart over time")
```
:::

## How these numbers are checked

<details class="more"><summary>Automatic checks, every route, every day</summary>

Our script runs two automatic checks every day, without anyone needing to go
out and watch the buses ([Methods](methods.qmd), section 5). The first check uses a
clue the feed already gives us. Each bus report names the stop the bus is
heading for, and that name switches to the next stop once the bus passes. If
our departure time lands between the last report naming a stop and the first
report naming a later one, give or take 30 seconds, it agrees with the feed.
The second check looks at the time it took to get from one stop to the next.
That time should never run backwards, and it should never mean the bus went
faster than 126 km/h (about 78 mph).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const val = latest?.validation;
  const feed = val?.feed_agreement, travel = val?.travel_times;
  if (!feed && !travel) return noDetail();
  const checks = [
    ["Inferred departures compared with the feed", count(feed?.compared)],
    ["Agree with the feed's change of stop (within 30 seconds)", pct(feed?.within_tolerance_share, 1)],
    ["Median time from inferred departure to the first report naming the next stop", unit(feed?.feed_change_after_departure_s?.median, "second", 1)],
    ["Times the feed's stop sequence went backwards within a trip", count(feed?.feed_sequence_going_backwards)],
    ["Segments between inferred times", count(travel?.segments)],
    ["Segments running backwards in time", count(travel?.negative)],
    ["Segments faster than 126 km/h (about 78 mph)", count(travel?.over_max_speed)],
  ].map(([check, value]) => ({check, value}));
  return ch.table(checks, {
    caption: `Results of the automatic checks for ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
    columns: [{key: "check", label: "Check", sortable: false}, {key: "value", label: "Result", align: "right", sortable: false}],
  });
}, "The automatic checks")
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Timed in person on route 60</summary>

To make sure our times match what really happens on the street, we time
buses in person and compare. The goal is for our times to be off by 30
seconds or less on average. So far we have done this only on route 60,
riding on board, so it doesn't yet cover other routes, buses leaving after they have
waited at a timepoint, or buses leaving a terminal. The two automatic checks
above still cover every route every day. The person timing the bus notes the
same moments our method looks for: when the bus comes within 40 meters
(about 130 feet) of the stop, and when it gets more than 40 meters past it. From on board, it is often
easier to note the moment the bus is level with the stop, and we compare
that with the midpoint of our two times.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
fc = json("data/ontime/field-check.json")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
guard(() => {
  const rows = [["All", fc?.overall], ["Arrivals (130 feet before the stop)", fc?.arrival], ["Departures (130 feet past the stop)", fc?.departure], ["Level with the stop", fc?.pass]]
    .filter(([, s]) => s?.n > 0)
    .map(([moment, s]) => ({moment, n: s.n, bias: s.bias_s, mae: s.mae_s, w30: s.within_30s_share, w60: s.within_60s_share}));
  if (rows.length === 0) {
    const waiting = fc?.rows_waiting_for_their_day;
    return html`<p>No timed observations have been scored yet${waiting ? `, and ${count(waiting)} ${waiting === 1 ? "is" : "are"} waiting for ${waiting === 1 ? "its" : "their"} day to be processed` : ""}.</p>`;
  }
  const target = fc.meets_target == null
    ? `The 30-second target is judged once there are ${fc.target_min_n ?? 5} timed moments.`
    : fc.meets_target ? "The average difference meets the 30-second target." : "The average difference has not yet met the 30-second target.";
  return html`<p>We have scored ${plural(fc.overall.n, "timed moment")} over ${plural(fc.days?.length ?? 0, "day")}.
      Each difference is our time minus the timed one, in seconds, so a positive bias means our times run late. ${target}</p>
    ${ch.table(rows, {
      caption: "How closely our times match times taken in person",
      columns: [
        {key: "moment", label: "Moment timed", sortable: false},
        {key: "n", label: "Timed", align: "right", format: count, sortable: false},
        {key: "bias", label: "Bias (seconds)", align: "right", format: v => num(v, 1), sortable: false},
        {key: "mae", label: "Mean absolute difference (seconds)", align: "right", format: v => num(v, 1), sortable: false},
        {key: "w30", label: "Within 30 seconds", align: "right", format: v => pct(v), sortable: false},
        {key: "w60", label: "Within 60 seconds", align: "right", format: v => pct(v), sortable: false},
      ],
    })}`;
}, "The in-person check")
```
